note: THE UNIVERSITY PROJECT MANIFEST — the declared set of projects the public hallway may render.
DECLARED, NOT DISCOVERED. This file is the whole allow-list. build_university.cjs walks ONLY
what is named here. A project that is not in this file does not appear in the hallway, cannot
be linked to, and cannot leak a path. That is the same rule generators/sources.json states for
the docs pipeline ('The generator reads nothing that is not declared here') and it exists for
the same reason: a discovery-based generator publishes whatever happens to be on the disk.
PRIVATE PROJECTS ARE DESCRIBED, NEVER READ. For visibility:private entries the generator
records name, one_line, languages, branch and head commit ONLY — it does not read file
contents, does not emit paths, and never produces a deep link. A private project renders as a
door you cannot open yet, with the reason stated.
MATURITY IS DECLARED BY A HUMAN, NOT INFERRED. A generator can measure whether a port answers;
it cannot measure whether a thing is finished. maturity here is an operator claim and the
hallway labels it as one. The measured facts (branch, commit, dirty count, languages) come from
the repository and carry the commit they were read at.
ABSENCE IS STATED, NEVER ASSERTED. Where a field cannot be established the generator emits an
explicit not-established marker. It never substitutes a plausible default. A fallback string is
a claim, and the else-branch is where false claims get authored unreviewed.
A PRIVATE WORKING REPOSITORY AND A PUBLIC SNAPSHOT ARE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, AND THE FIRST
VERSION OF THIS FILE COLLAPSED THEM. Three projects here are developed in a private repository
AND ALSO have a public, redacted, frozen snapshot published under another name. Declaring only
visibility:private made the hallway print 'this repository is not public yet, so this door cannot
be opened' over a door that does open -- false, and published for roughly an hour on 2026-08-24.
So a snapshot is declared separately from visibility, and it carries WHAT IT IS: frozen, taken on
a stated date, a stated number of commits, no history. The commit in the citation is the PRIVATE
working commit the bytes were read at; it does not exist in the snapshot, and the door says so
rather than emitting a deep link that would 404.
A MIRROR AND A FROZEN SNAPSHOT ARE DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE DOOR MUST SAY WHICH. On 2026-08-24
the operator ruled the snapshots into real mirrors: a live public repository that tracks the
private one by promotion, one commit per promotion, each recording the private commit it came
from, merged by a human through a pull request. Two have been promoted and merged; one has an
open pull request and is still frozen. `public_mirror.kind` carries that distinction, because
'frozen since 2026-08-02' and 'updated today' are not the same promise to a reader, and rendering
them identically is how a stale link keeps its credibility.

maturity_vocabulary.running: a process answers on a port, or a deployed URL responds, right now
maturity_vocabulary.built: code exists and runs when started; nothing is answering at read time
maturity_vocabulary.design-only: specified in documents; the code does not exist yet
maturity_vocabulary.contradicted: was tried and the evidence went against it — kept visible on purpose
maturity_vocabulary.archived: superseded or duplicated by another entry; retained for history

projects.title: The ORCHESTRATE Active Inference Workbench
projects.one_line: A pedagogical BEAM-native active-inference workbench: discrete-time POMDP with mean-field variational message passing and an expected-free-energy-weighted policy posterior, plus a 10-chapter curriculum, a visual model builder, and browser learning labs.
projects.why_it_is_here: It is the teaching faculty. It already holds a working model builder, a four-level learning ladder and a runnable cookbook — the University links to it rather than rebuilding it.

projects.title: UNI.MineCraft — the colony
projects.one_line: A pure-Elixir categorical active-inference colony: embodied agents living in a real Minecraft world, each running one mean-field predict-act tick as its life, with a broadcast platform built over it.
projects.why_it_is_here: It is the world where the agents actually live, and the home of the Function Designer Card that compiles a declarative model description into a runnable brain.

projects.title: UNI-FLAGELLUM — the science instrument
projects.one_line: A CPU-only digital-organ laboratory that keeps a bacterial flagellar-motor world process strictly separate from the active-inference agent that models it.
projects.why_it_is_here: It is where a claim meets a real measured organism, and where the estate keeps a result that went against it in plain view.

projects.title: The UNI Encyclopedia & Cookbook
projects.one_line: An encyclopedia and a literal cookbook of buildable recipes across a developmental ladder, governed by two sovereign ledgers that never let a nature citation count as a UNI result.
projects.why_it_is_here: Its two-ledger discipline is the honesty model the whole University adopts: what UNI has earned and what nature has shown are different registers and are never merged.

projects.title: UNI.Public — the documentation estate
projects.one_line: The public technical documentation of the estate, where every volatile number is generated from the repository it describes and carries the commit it was read from.
projects.why_it_is_here: It is the shell this University is built into, and the reason every number on these pages can be traced rather than trusted.

projects.title: The UNI Campus — universalnaturalintelligence.com

live.note: the public front door: five hands-on labs, the Sensorium, Gentle Entry, a history of inference, the Cookbook and both books

projects.one_line: The public front door of the estate: the Precision, Echo, Loop, Heart and Cell labs, the Sensorium, Gentle Entry, a history of inference, and the published Cookbook — in ten languages.
projects.why_it_is_here: It is where a visitor first touches the mathematics — a lab in the browser within a minute, no install, no account — and every deeper door on this site leads back to code.

projects.title: The Bayes Museum — 50 exhibits
projects.one_line: Fifty small exhibits of Bayesian reasoning in everyday clothes — weather, health, security, science — each one a single idea a visitor can hold.
projects.why_it_is_here: It is the breadth wing of the teaching faculty: where the labs go deep on one model, the museum goes wide across fifty. It has no public repository yet, and this door says so rather than hiding it.
